person.name: Alvar_Aalto
person.summary: Alvar Aalto was a Finnish architect and designer whose buildings, furniture, glassware, and interiors joined modern construction with natural materials and human comfort. Working with Aino Aalto and later Elissa Aalto, he designed projects ranging from tuberculosis sanatoria and libraries to civic centers and private houses.

conclusion: Alvar Aalto designed buildings, interiors, furniture, glassware, textiles, sculptures, and paintings. His work joined buildings with their furnishings, materials, and light. His bent plywood furniture influenced later designers including Charles and Ray Eames and George Nelson.

events.title: Birth in Kuortane
events.description: Hugo Alvar Henrik Aalto was born in Kuortane, Finland. His father, Johan Henrik Aalto, worked as a Finnish-speaking land surveyor. His mother, Selma Matilda Hackstedt, was a Swedish-speaking postmistress.

events.title: Graduates in Architecture
events.description: Alvar Aalto graduated in architecture from the Helsinki University of Technology in Helsinki. His studies had paused during the Finnish Civil War. He fought with the White Army in the 1918 conflict.

Finnish Civil War.explanation: The 1918 conflict divided Finland between the White Army and the Red Guards. It took place during Aalto’s architectural studies.

events.background:
While still enrolled, Aalto designed and built a house for his parents in Alajärvi. It was his first architectural work.

He began military service in the summer of 1922. He completed reserve officer training at Hamina. He was promoted to reserve second lieutenant in June 1923.

background_images.caption: Main building of the reserve officers school, Hamina, Finland. Completed in 1898. Architect: Jac. Ahrenberg.
background_images.creator: Pitkäkaula

events.title: Opens Jyväskylä Office
events.description: Alvar Aalto opened an architectural office in Jyväskylä under the name Alvar Aalto, Architect and Monumental Artist. He designed small single-family houses and other local projects. He also wrote about architecture for the Jyväskylä newspaper Sisä-Suomi.

events.title: Marries Aino Marsio
events.description: Alvar Aalto married architect Aino Marsio in Jyväskylä. They had met as architecture students. They traveled through northern Italy for their honeymoon and studied its buildings, art, and urban spaces.

events.title: Moves Practice to Turku
events.description: Alvar Aalto won the competition for the Southwest Finland Agricultural Cooperative building. He and Aino Aalto moved their practice from Jyväskylä to Turku. In Turku, they worked with architect Erik Bryggman on projects including the Turku Fair, an architectural exhibition.

events.title: Designs Paimio Sanatorium
events.description: Alvar Aalto and Aino Aalto designed Paimio Sanatorium in Paimio for patients with tuberculosis. They planned its wards, terraces, colors, and lighting around routines of treatment and rest. They also designed furniture and interiors for patients’ daily use.

images.caption: Paimio Sanatorium, designed by Alvar Aalto
images.creator: V. K. Hietanen

events.background:
The commission brought together ideas Aalto had been testing in Turku and on his European travels. The plan used splayed wings, a form associated with Jan Duiker’s Zonnestraal Sanatorium in the Netherlands. Aalto had visited Zonnestraal while it was under construction.

The building also became a full-scale interior-design project. Aino Aalto concentrated on furniture and interiors. The Aaltos developed furniture and lamps for the rooms as part of the building’s equipment. One result was the Paimio Chair. Its cantilevered birch frame required wood bends that tested the manufacturing techniques then available. The chair entered the permanent collections of the Museum of Modern Art in New York and the Finnish Design Museum.

Completed in 1932, Paimio was among the works that first brought Aalto international attention.

background_images.caption: The Paimio Sanatorium, designed by the Finnish architect Alvar Aalto, served as a former tuberculosis hospital in Paimio, Southwestern Finland.
background_images.creator: V. K. Hietanen

events.title: Creates Paimio Chair
events.description: Alvar Aalto and Aino Aalto developed the Paimio Chair for patients at Paimio Sanatorium. Its frame used laminated birch bent into a continuous curve. Its reclining seat supported people who spent long periods seated during treatment.

event_class.title: Paimio Chair
event_class.description: A cantilevered chair uses a laminated birch frame and curved plywood seat to support a reclining sitter.
event_class.impact: Aalto’s bent plywood furniture had a profound influence on the furniture designs of Charles and Ray Eames and George Nelson.

events.title: Completes Viipuri Library
events.description: Alvar Aalto completed Viipuri Library in Viipuri after eight years of design and construction. He equipped the reading rooms with skylights and warm materials. He gave the lecture hall a wave-shaped wooden ceiling.

events.title: Founds Artek
events.description: Alvar Aalto founded Artek in Helsinki with Aino Aalto, Maire Gullichsen, and Nils-Gustav Hahl. Artek was a furniture company that promoted the Aaltos’ furniture and glassware. It produced furnishings for their buildings, including lighting and interior objects.
events.background:
Maire Gullichsen wanted to establish a Helsinki gallery for modern art. Interest in Aalto furniture had also grown in England. The company’s name joined “art” and “technology.” It expressed Bauhaus-linked ideals of skilled production and careful materials.

Furniture had previously been manufactured in Turku by Huonekalu-ja Rakennustyötehdas Oy. Artek gave the group a way to coordinate interiors with the Aaltos’ architectural projects. Hahl ran the company and its art program. Aino directed its artistic work. She set early furniture standards and oversaw commissions for lighting, textiles, screens, and household objects. Her first Artek interior commission was the Viipuri Library in 1936. Under her leadership, the company completed more than eighty interiors.

events.title: Completes Villa Mairea
events.description: Alvar Aalto completed Villa Mairea near Noormarkku for Maire and Harry Gullichsen. He and architect Aino Aalto designed the house and its interiors. They also designed its furniture, lighting, and garden. Maire Gullichsen took a close role in the interior work.

events.title: Teaches at MIT
events.description: Alvar Aalto taught at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in Cambridge, Massachusetts, from 1940 to 1948. The appointment brought his architectural practice into an American university setting during the war years.

events.title: Completes Baker House
events.description: Alvar Aalto completed Baker House, a student residence at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in Cambridge. Its curved plan gave residents views from rooms along the Charles River. The shape also improved ventilation.

events.title: Completes Säynätsalo Town Hall
events.description: Alvar Aalto completed Säynätsalo Town Hall in Säynätsalo. Elissa Aalto served as supervising architect during construction. The complex placed the council chamber and offices around a raised brick courtyard. It also included a library, shops, and apartments.

events.title: Marries Elissa Mäkiniemi
events.description: Alvar Aalto married architect Elissa Mäkiniemi in Finland. Mäkiniemi had joined Aalto’s office in 1949. She supervised construction on major projects there.

events.title: Completes Finlandia Hall
events.description: Alvar Aalto completed Finlandia Hall in Helsinki as a concert and congress building on Töölö Bay. The building used white Carrara marble and dark granite. Its interiors were lined with wood. A high tower contained the main auditorium.

Carrara marble.explanation: Carrara marble is a white stone quarried in the Carrara area of Italy. Aalto used it as a prominent exterior material for Finlandia Hall.

events.background:
Finlandia Hall grew out of Aalto’s plan for the empty central area between Töölö Bay and Helsinki’s extensive railway yards. He presented the plan in 1961 and revised it several times during the early 1960s. Aalto proposed a row of separate marble-clad cultural buildings facing the water. The plan included an opera house, a museum of architecture, and headquarters for the Finnish Academy.

The proposal also continued into the Kamppi district with a group of tall office blocks. Only two parts of the larger scheme were built. Finlandia Hall stood on the bay side of the project. An office building for the Helsinki Electricity Company was completed in Kamppi in 1975.

background_images.caption: The Finlandia Hall is a congress and event venue in the centre of Helsinki on the Töölönlahti Bay, owned by the City of Helsinki.
background_images.creator: Ninara

events.title: Dies in Helsinki
events.description: Alvar Aalto died in Helsinki on 11 May 1976. He was buried at Hietaniemi Cemetery in Helsinki.
